M12-01-DEALROOM.2: In {B_EBITDA_NORM} normalised EBITDA: the one reported in the accounts, adjusted for the two costs a buyer won't bear (section 1).
M12-01-DEALROOM.3: In {B_EV} the Enterprise Value paid, at the agreed entry multiple.
M12-01-DEALROOM.4: In {B_PREZZO_EQ} what the seller receives for their shares.
M12-01-DEALROOM.5: In {B_FEE} the transaction fees in euros.
M12-01-DEALROOM.6: In {B_IMPIEGHI} total uses: all the money needed at closing. The deal is cash free / debt free: the existing debt doesn't stay in the company.
M12-01-DEALROOM.7: In {B_DEBITO} the senior debt raised, at the leverage agreed with the banks.
M12-01-DEALROOM.8: In {B_SPONSOR} the equity the sponsor must put in to close the sources.
M12-01-DEALROOM.9: Row {ROW_EBITDA}, {p1}: each year's EBITDA, growing at the assumed rate. A single formula, copied across the whole row.
M12-01-DEALROOM.10: Row {ROW_INTERESSI}: the year's interest, calculated on opening debt (i.e. the previous year's closing debt): this keeps the model free of circularity.
M12-01-DEALROOM.11: Row {ROW_CASSA}: the cash available to repay debt, i.e. EBITDA converted to cash per the assumption, after paying interest.
M12-01-DEALROOM.12: Row {ROW_RIMBORSO}: repayment with a 100% cash sweep. All available cash goes to repay debt, but you can't repay more than the debt that's left.
M12-01-DEALROOM.14: In {B_EV_OUT} the Enterprise Value at exit, at the end of year {ANNI}, at the assumed exit multiple.
M12-01-DEALROOM.15: In {B_EQ_OUT} the value of the sponsor's equity at exit.
M12-01-DEALROOM.16: In {B_MOIC} the sponsor's multiple on invested capital (MoIC).
M12-01-DEALROOM.17: In {B_IRR} the sponsor's IRR. A single contribution at entry and a single receipt at exit: MoIC and holding period ({B_ANNI}) are enough.
M12-01-DEALROOM.18: In {B_DECISIONE} the recommendation to the committee, calculated and not typed by hand: "INVEST" if the IRR reaches at least the hurdle ({B_HURDLE}), otherwise "PASS". If an assumption changes, the recommendation must update on its own.
M12-01-DEALROOM.19:
## Live Deal Room — the committee is waiting

The sponsor wants to buy 100% of an industrial company through a leveraged buyout. You have all the data in the sheet: build the model from start to finish and bring a recommendation to the committee. No formulas suggested: the mandate says what's needed, the how is up to you (hints are available, but they cost XP).

### 1. Quality of Earnings
Reported EBITDA bears the departing owner's excess compensation and one-off legal costs that won't recur: they need to be added back.

### 2. Sources & Uses
The price is {p0} normalised EBITDA. The deal is **cash free / debt free**: the sponsor pays the equity to the seller and refinances all the existing net debt in full; fees come on top. The banks lend {p1} normalised EBITDA at {p2}; the sponsor puts in the rest.

### 3. Repayment plan
Five years, EBITDA growing {p3} a year. {p4} of EBITDA becomes cash before interest (after taxes, capex and working capital); everything left after interest goes to repay debt (**100% cash sweep**).

### 4. Exit and decision
Exit at the end of year {ANNI} at {p6} EBITDA. The committee invests only if the IRR reaches at least {p7}.

Order of magnitude to get your bearings: reported EBITDA {p8}.
